<time_normalization_instructions>
  Parse time ranges into ISO 8601 format. Handle various formats:
  
  <format_examples>
    <example>
      <input>Year ranges: "1996-2007"</input>
      <output>start: 1996-01-01T00:00:00Z, end: 2007-12-31T23:59:59Z</output>
    </example>
    <example>
      <input>Date ranges: "Aug 21, 2017"</input>
      <output>specific dates</output>
    </example>
    <example>
      <input>Time ranges: "16:00 UT to 19:00 UT on 2017 August 21"</input>
      <output>specific times</output>
    </example>
    <example>
      <input>Unclear: "Unclear"</input>
      <output>mark as approximate with null dates</output>
    </example>
    <example>
      <input>Single‐timestamp events</input>
      <output>set both start and end to that exact ISO instant</output>
    </example>
    <example>
      <input>Missing date context: "19:02:58–19:10:20 UT"</input>
      <output>set error: true, error_message: "Cannot determine date - time range lacks date context"</output>
    </example>
  </format_examples>

  <critical_requirements>
    <requirement>If date information is missing and you cannot determine the date, set error: true with a descriptive error_message</requirement>
    <requirement>NEVER default to Unix epoch (1970-01-01) - this indicates a parsing failure</requirement>
    <requirement>When in doubt about dates, it's better to return an error than to guess incorrectly</requirement>
  </critical_requirements>

  <precision_levels>
    Set precision level based on specificity: year, month, day, hour, minute, second
  </precision_levels>
</time_normalization_instructions>

<user_prompt>
  Parse this time range: "More than 10 years (dates not specified in the paper)"
  
  Convert to ISO format and determine precision level.
</user_prompt>

Please supply a reference start or end date if you want concrete ISO timestamps. If you want this represented as an interval length only, specify how to anchor it (e.g., end date or start date)."}
